qualification: In two exploratory static-camera runs the localization adapter remained TRACKING; this does not disprove the single propagated_from_future lock in #273 or identify its cause. No health threshold was changed.
verified_findings: Low-load #274: 694/695 status samples were valid TRACKING after one initial waiting_for_propagated sample. External raw propagated-odometry source-age-at-receipt was -2 to +2 ms; none exceeded the 20 ms future tolerance. RTF was 0.9652.

Mapping/EGO #275: 695/695 status samples were valid TRACKING, with no propagated_from_future latch. External probe clock estimates had three early samples below -20 ms and a minimum -297 ms while its receipt gaps reached 714.7 ms; adapter status remained valid and its last published propagated output age was 3 ms. Treat these probe-clock estimates as scheduling-sensitive, not adapter input ages.

Under #275 load the observed simulation clock rate was 0.7217. EGO logged repeated 1.0 s odom/depth timeouts while localization remained TRACKING; however, the launch used odometry_topic:=odom although the adapter publishes /localization/optimized_imu_odom. This is a topic-wiring defect in the diagnostic setup, not evidence about EGO freshness with the correct input.
#273 had one propagated_from_future lock 143 ms after its saved snapshot; #274/#275 did not reproduce it. A causal claim is not supported.
limitations: Both runs used a static D435i and no truth, PX4, controller, or goal client; neither tested motion accuracy, map coverage, navigation, or flight.

The independent freshness probe receives /clock on its own executor; under #275 load its callback lagged. It cannot prove which exact clock value the localization adapter read for a given DDS message.
The comparison is unpaired and exploratory; no threshold adjustment or GOAL B/P2 acceptance follows from it.
The #275 EGO odometry remap was incorrect (odom vs /localization/optimized_imu_odom); its EGO timeout logs are excluded from planner-input conclusions.
